entities.text:
High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 At Jabalpur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Shri Ashutosh Tiwari - Advocate for the appellant.
Shri Amit Pandey - Government Advocate for the responde

Heard on I.A. No.17388/2025 , first application under Section 389(1) of Cr.P.C./Section 430(1) of BNSS, for suspension of sentence and grant of bail filed on behalf of the appellant.
2.

This appeal has been preferred against the judgment dated 31.07.2021 passed by Special Judge,
POCSO Act, District Balaghat (M.P.) in S.T. No.SC ATR No.49/2019, whereby the appellant has been convicted and sentenced as under:
Conviction U/s. Imprisonment Fine

entities.text:
Special Judge,
POCSO Act, District Balaghat (M.P.)
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
In lieu of fine 376(2)(n) of IPC and S. 5(L)/6 of R.I. for 10 Additional R.I. for Rs.5000/-
POCSO Act years three years  R.I. for 20   376(3) of IPC Rs.10,000  years  3.
Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the trial Court has wrongly convicted and sentenced the appellant.
As per prosecution case, the allegation against the appellant is that he committed sexual intercourse with a minor girl who is aged about 14 years and is of unsound mind.
Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the trial Court has not appreciated the evidence properly.

There was a consensual relationship between the prosecutrix and the appellant and when it came to the knowledge of the parents of prosecutrix that she is pregnant, a false case has been registered 2 CRA-12008-2022 against the appellant.
Learned counsel further submits that trial Court in paragraph 50 of the impugned judgment has found that the prosecutrix is of sound mind.
The prosecution has failed to prove the case beyond reasonable doubt.
There are material contradictions and omissions in the testimonies of the prosecution witnesses.
He has already undergone almost three years of incarceration, therefore, the application may be considered on the ground of period of incarceration.
This appeal is of the year 2022 and there is no possibility of early hearing of the appeal in near future.

1 abide by the directions and conditions, which may be imposed by this Court.

sentences.text:
Hence,
it is prayed that the application for suspension of sentence may be allowed.

4 .
Learned counsel for the State on the other hand has opposed the application for suspension of sentence and supported the impugned judgment of conviction and sentence passed by the trial Court.
5. Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.

6 . Considering the arguments advanced by learned counsel for the parties and the overall facts and circumstances of the case, we are of the opinion that the application for suspension of sentence and grant of bail to the appellant can be considered.

7. Accordingly, without commenting anything on the merits of the case, I.A.
No.17388/2025 is allowed.

8 . It is directed that subject to depositing the fine amount, if not already deposited,
the remaining jail sentence of the appellant is hereby suspended and he be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond in the sum of 3 CRA-12008-2022 Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with one solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court with a further direction to appear before the Registry of this Court on 18.02.2026 and on such other dates, as may be fixed by the Registry in this regard during pendency of this appeal.
9. List the matter for final hearing in due course.
 (VIVEK KUMAR SINGH) (AJAY KUMAR   JUDGE JUDG  Shanu Amar @ Raja vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 6 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/2412730/
